text:
Sources support differential testing beyond repeatability. PyTorch’s [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.rnn.GRU.html) imply that zero embeddings alone do not make padding inert: biases can update hidden states. Derived diagnostic: compare identical histories with different amounts of left padding against an unpadded, explicit recurrence that skips padding, matching PyTorch’s gate ordering and reset-gate placement. Compare each valid recurrent state, then readout, then candidate scores to locate the first divergence. Select the final nonpadding index, never count−1. Test singleton versus mixed batches, batch permutations, duplicated rows, and A→B→A calls with fresh initial states. [GRU4Rec’s implementation audit](https://hidasi.eu/gru4rec_third_party_comparison/exp_impl/gru4rec_pytorch/gru4rec_pytorch_main.html) documents actual hidden-state reset defects.

[PyTorch numerical-accuracy documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) warns that batched and sliced computations can differ numerically; bitwise batch invariance is therefore too strict. Use evaluation mode, disable mixed precision/TF32 for diagnosis, and compare against an FP64 explicit recurrence with identical weights. Report absolute/relative state and score errors by timestep, length and batch composition. FP64 agreement is evidence, not proof. Following [checkpoint-loading guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html), reconstruct the saved architecture, load strictly, call eval(), and compare training-side versus generated predictor preprocessing, item mappings, states and scores on identical inputs.

Derived stability bound: if every candidate score has certified absolute error ≤ε, top-10 membership is unchanged when s₍₁₀₎−s₍₁₁₎>2ε; any pair separated by >2ε preserves order. For dot-product scoring with unchanged item vectors, |Δsᵢ|≤‖eᵢ‖₂‖Δh‖₂, plus scoring-roundoff error. Empirical maximum discrepancies provide sensitivity checks, not universal certificates; near-boundary cases and ties require explicit reporting.
